description: Machine-readable inventory of security audit checks: access control and sessions, untrusted input and output, secrets, data, and browser hardening, and large-language-model features.

statusTaxonomy.partial: The invariant mostly holds, with exceptions; or a hardening control is missing without a concrete failure scenario; or a soft check shows mixed adherence.
statusTaxonomy.violation: Concrete code or configuration breaks the invariant. A model-judged weakness also names an attacker-controlled entry point, a path across a security boundary, and an impact.

enrichmentFlags.description: Scan Git history with gitleaks, and run Semgrep and the project's configured ESLint security rules when installed, to confirm and extend findings.

checks.title: Server entry points authenticate the caller
checks.rationale: Server Actions and route handlers are public HTTP endpoints, so one that skips the session check lets anyone on the internet call it.
checks.expectation: Every Server Action, route handler, API route, and loader or action that is not deliberately public verifies the session itself, with a verified token (never a decoded-only one), before it reads or changes data.
checks.violationSignal: An entry point that reads or changes non-public data with no session verification of its own, reported with the entry point and what an anonymous caller can do.

checks.title: Each request is authorized for the records it touches
checks.rationale: An authenticated user who can change an identifier in a request can read or change every other user's records.
checks.expectation: Every query or mutation that takes a record identifier from the request scopes it to the caller (owner, tenant, or role) on the server, and privileged operations check the caller's role.
checks.violationSignal: A lookup or mutation by a request-supplied identifier with no ownership, tenant, or role condition, reported with the entry point and the query.

checks.title: Authorization does not rely on middleware alone
checks.rationale: Middleware is skipped by matcher gaps and was bypassable outright in vulnerable Next.js versions (CVE-2025-29927), so it cannot be the only gate.
checks.expectation: Middleware or proxy checks are an optimistic first pass; the page, Server Action, or route handler, or the data-access layer it calls, enforces the same rule again.
checks.violationSignal: Protected data or mutations whose only check is in middleware or a proxy file, reported with the matcher and the unguarded entry point.

checks.title: State changes resist cross-site requests
checks.rationale: A state change that a cross-site page can trigger with the victim's cookies acts on the victim's behalf without their intent.
checks.expectation: State changes use non-GET methods; cookie-authenticated route handlers rely on SameSite=Lax or Strict cookies or check the Origin header; Server Action allowed origins are not widened to arbitrary sites.
checks.violationSignal: A GET handler that changes state, or a cookie-authenticated mutation reachable cross-site (SameSite=None, or wildcard allowed origins) with no origin or token check.

checks.title: Hand-written sign-in flows use state, PKCE, and nonce
checks.rationale: A hand-built OAuth or OpenID Connect flow without these parameters allows login cross-site request forgery, code interception, or token replay.
checks.expectation: Hand-written OAuth flows send and verify a `state` value and use PKCE; OpenID Connect flows also send and verify a `nonce`. Not applicable when a maintained library runs the flow or there is no OAuth flow.
checks.violationSignal: A hand-written authorization request or callback that omits or does not verify `state`, PKCE, or `nonce`.

checks.title: Session tokens stay out of web storage
checks.rationale: Any script on the page can read web storage, so one cross-site scripting flaw becomes a stolen session.
checks.expectation: Session and access tokens live in HttpOnly cookies, not in localStorage or sessionStorage.
checks.violationSignal: A session, access, or refresh token written to or read from localStorage or sessionStorage.

checks.title: Session cookies are Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite
checks.rationale: A session cookie without these flags can be read by scripts, sent over plain HTTP, or attached to cross-site requests.
checks.expectation: Cookies that carry a session or token are set with Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite=Lax or Strict, either explicitly or by a library whose defaults set them.
checks.violationSignal: A session or token cookie set without HttpOnly, without Secure, or with SameSite=None and no other protection.

checks.title: Tokens and password hashes use strong cryptography
checks.rationale: Predictable tokens can be guessed, and fast or unsalted password hashes are cracked as soon as the database leaks.
checks.expectation: Session, reset, and invitation tokens come from a cryptographically secure generator; passwords are hashed with bcrypt, scrypt, or Argon2; signed tokens are verified with a pinned algorithm.
checks.violationSignal: `Math.random()` used for a security token, MD5 or SHA-1 or a single unsalted SHA-256 for passwords, or a token verifier that accepts any algorithm.

checks.title: Server entry points validate their input
checks.rationale: Unvalidated input lets callers write fields they should not (mass assignment) and turns type confusion into logic flaws.
checks.expectation: Every Server Action and route handler parses its arguments, form data, JSON body, and parameters with a schema on the server, and passes only the allowed fields on.
checks.violationSignal: An entry point that passes request data to a query, mutation, or downstream call without server-side parsing, or spreads a whole request body into a write.

checks.title: Queries and commands are parameterised
checks.rationale: Request data concatenated into SQL, a shell command, or a file path lets an attacker run their own query or command.
checks.expectation: Database queries use parameters or a query builder, shell commands take argument arrays, and file paths from requests are resolved and confined to an allowed directory.
checks.violationSignal: Request data reaching a raw query (`$queryRawUnsafe`, `sql.raw`, string-built SQL), `exec` or a shell, or a filesystem path without parameterisation or confinement.

checks.title: Server requests do not follow user-supplied URLs
checks.rationale: A server that fetches a URL the caller chooses can be pointed at cloud metadata, internal services, and localhost.
checks.expectation: Server-side requests go to fixed hosts, or validate the parsed URL against an allowlist of schemes and hosts and refuse redirects to other hosts.
checks.violationSignal: A user-supplied URL or host reaching `fetch`, an HTTP client, or an image or PDF renderer on the server without an allowlist.

checks.title: dangerouslySetInnerHTML renders only sanitized HTML
checks.rationale: HTML rendered without sanitization runs any script an attacker can place in it, in every viewer's session.
checks.expectation: Every `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` renders constant HTML, or content passed through DOMPurify or an equivalent sanitizer on the way in.
checks.violationSignal: A `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` whose HTML can contain user-controlled, stored, or fetched content with no sanitizer on the path.

checks.title: Other HTML sinks receive only sanitized content
checks.rationale: Raw DOM writes and HTML-enabled Markdown bypass React's escaping exactly as `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` does.
checks.expectation: `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, `insertAdjacentHTML`, `document.write`, and Markdown or rich-text renderers with raw HTML enabled receive only constant or sanitized content.
checks.violationSignal: One of these sinks receiving user-controlled, stored, or fetched content without sanitization.

checks.title: User-supplied URLs use safe schemes
checks.rationale: A `javascript:` or `data:` URL in a link, frame, or navigation runs script when it is followed.
checks.expectation: URLs from users or stored data that reach `href`, `src`, `formAction`, `window.open`, or `location` are parsed and limited to `https:`, `http:`, `mailto:`, or relative paths.
checks.violationSignal: A user-controlled URL reaching one of these sinks with no scheme check, where the React version or framework does not already block `javascript:` URLs for that sink.

checks.title: Redirects go only to allowed destinations
checks.rationale: An open redirect on a trusted domain makes phishing links convincing and can leak authorization codes or tokens.
checks.expectation: Redirect targets from query parameters, form fields, or sign-in callbacks are limited to same-origin paths or an allowlist, checked after URL parsing so `//host` and backslash forms are refused.
checks.violationSignal: A `redirect()`, `router.push`, `location` assignment, or callback URL that uses a request-supplied destination without such a check.

checks.title: No eval or new Function
checks.rationale: Running strings as code turns any attacker-influenced text into code execution and forces a Content Security Policy to allow 'unsafe-eval'.
checks.expectation: Shipped source never calls `eval`, `new Function`, `Function` with a string, or string-form `setTimeout` and `setInterval`.
checks.violationSignal: Any such call outside tests, cited by line. The collector decides presence; the model traces whether attacker-influenced text reaches it.

checks.title: Message listeners check the sender's origin
checks.rationale: Any site that can open or frame the page can post messages to it, so a listener that skips the origin check obeys attackers.
checks.expectation: Every `message` event listener checks `event.origin` against an exact allowlist before reading `event.data`, and every `postMessage` names a target origin rather than `*` when the data is sensitive.
checks.violationSignal: A listener that acts on `event.data` without an exact origin check, or sensitive data posted to `*`.

checks.title: No secrets in source
checks.rationale: A committed secret is usable by anyone who can read the repository or any clone of it, and stays in Git history after it is deleted.
checks.expectation: Tracked files contain no credential in a high-confidence format (cloud, payment, source-control, chat, and model-provider keys, private keys, database URLs with passwords), and committed environment files assign no real value to a secret-named variable. With `--with-scan`, gitleaks finds none in Git history either.
checks.violationSignal: A credential in a tracked file, cited with its value redacted, or gitleaks findings in history.

checks.title: Local environment files are ignored by Git
checks.rationale: Local environment files hold real secrets, and without an ignore rule the first `git add .` commits them.
checks.expectation: A rule in the repository's own `.gitignore` covers `.env`, `.env.local`, and `.env.*.local` in every application folder, except environment files the team commits on purpose.
checks.violationSignal: No repository ignore rule for these files, or coverage only from a personal or global ignore file.

checks.title: Public environment variables hold no secrets
checks.rationale: Variables with a public prefix such as `NEXT_PUBLIC_` or `VITE_` are inlined into the JavaScript every visitor downloads.
checks.expectation: Only values designed to be public (publishable keys, public identifiers, URLs) use a public prefix.
checks.violationSignal: A secret, private key, service-role key, or server token exposed through a public-prefixed variable.

checks.title: Server secrets never reach client code
checks.rationale: A secret passed to a client component, returned from a Server Action, or added to the client build is shipped to every browser.
checks.expectation: Modules that read secrets import `server-only`; secrets are never passed as props to client components, returned from Server Actions or route handlers, or added to the build's client `env`.
checks.violationSignal: A secret value that reaches a client component, a response, or the client bundle. A secret-reading module without `server-only` but with no concrete leak is partial.

checks.title: Logs record no secrets or tokens
checks.rationale: Tokens and credentials in logs are readable by everyone with log access and by every log vendor.
checks.expectation: Code never passes tokens, passwords, secret environment values, or whole request headers or cookies to `console`, a logger, or an error reporter.
checks.violationSignal: A log or error-report call that includes a token, password, secret value, or full headers or cookies.

checks.title: Personal data stays out of URLs and analytics
checks.rationale: Personal data in URLs lands in history, logs, and referrers, and in analytics it is shared with a third party.
checks.expectation: Routes and links do not carry email addresses, phone numbers, government identifiers, or tokens, and analytics events do not include them. Soft check — mixed adherence is reported as partial.
checks.violationSignal: Personal data or tokens in a URL path or query, or in an analytics event payload.

checks.title: A Content Security Policy restricts scripts
checks.rationale: A strict policy stops most injected scripts from running, so one missed sanitizer does not become account takeover.
checks.expectation: A Content Security Policy is sent on HTML responses, and its `script-src` uses nonces, hashes, or `strict-dynamic` without `unsafe-inline`, `unsafe-eval`, or wildcard sources.
checks.violationSignal: No policy, or a policy whose `script-src` allows `unsafe-inline`, `unsafe-eval`, or any host. Without a concrete injection path it is a hardening gap, graded partial or missing.

checks.title: Other sites cannot frame the application
checks.rationale: A page that any site can frame can be overlaid to trick users into clicking (clickjacking).
checks.expectation: HTML responses send `frame-ancestors` in the Content Security Policy, or `X-Frame-Options: DENY` or `SAMEORIGIN`, unless embedding is a product requirement.
checks.violationSignal: Neither header on pages that perform actions, with no embedding requirement.

checks.title: HTTPS is enforced
checks.rationale: Plain HTTP exposes sessions and data on the network and lets an attacker rewrite responses.
checks.expectation: Production traffic is redirected to HTTPS with Strict-Transport-Security (a long `max-age`), set by the application or documented as set by the platform, and code requests no `http://` URLs outside local development.
checks.violationSignal: No HTTPS redirect or HSTS from the application or a documented platform default, or `http://` requests in production code.

checks.title: Baseline security headers are set
checks.rationale: These headers close small leaks (MIME sniffing, full referrer URLs, unused browser features) cheaply.
checks.expectation: HTML responses send `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, a `Referrer-Policy` of `strict-origin-when-cross-origin` or stricter, and a `Permissions-Policy` that disables unused features.
checks.violationSignal: One or more of these headers missing or set to a permissive value.

checks.title: Third-party scripts and frames are constrained
checks.rationale: A third-party script runs with the page's full authority, and an unsandboxed frame can navigate or prompt the user.
checks.expectation: Scripts loaded from other origins at fixed versions carry `integrity`, or are loaded through the framework's script component from a vendor the team accepts; third-party iframes use the narrowest `sandbox` and `allow` they need.
checks.violationSignal: A pinned third-party script without `integrity`, or a third-party iframe without `sandbox` that does not need full permissions.

checks.title: Model tool calls act only with the user's permissions
checks.rationale: Anyone who can put text in front of the model, including through retrieved documents, can make it call tools, so a tool that skips authorization is a public endpoint.
checks.expectation: Every tool a model can call validates its arguments with a schema, runs with the end user's identity and the same ownership checks as the equivalent endpoint, and requires explicit user confirmation for destructive or financial actions.
checks.violationSignal: A tool that reads or changes records by a model-supplied identifier without scoping to the user, or that performs a destructive or financial action without confirmation.

checks.title: Model output is never rendered as raw HTML
checks.rationale: Prompt injection controls model output, so rendering it as HTML is cross-site scripting by proxy.
checks.expectation: Model output is rendered as text, or through a Markdown renderer with raw HTML disabled and link schemes restricted.
checks.violationSignal: Model output reaching `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `innerHTML`, or a Markdown renderer with raw HTML enabled.

checks.title: Prompts carry no secrets or other users' data
checks.rationale: Anything in a prompt can be extracted by prompt injection, so a secret or another user's data in context is one question away from disclosure.
checks.expectation: Prompts and system messages contain no keys, internal URLs with credentials, or data the current user is not allowed to see; retrieved content is scoped to the user.
checks.violationSignal: A secret, credential, or another user's personal data placed in a prompt, system message, or retrieval context.

checks.title: Model usage is bounded per user
checks.rationale: An unbounded model endpoint lets one caller run up the bill or exhaust the provider quota for everyone.
checks.expectation: Model endpoints require a session, apply a per-user rate limit, cap output tokens and tool-call steps, and limit input size.
checks.violationSignal: A model endpoint with no rate limit, no output-token cap, or unbounded tool-call loops.
